caption:
Resolution gets the attention. Revisit cadence is what actually decides whether a system sees anything useful.

A sharper image of a location from four days ago tells you nothing about what changed there yesterday. Encroachment, a burn scar, a new access track, a flood edge — all of it can appear and vanish inside a single gap between passes. Tighter pixels don't buy back time you didn't collect.

The collection plan has to weigh revisit against resolution for the specific target, not chase the sharpest picture available. A coarser image every two days beats a crisp one every two weeks if the thing you're watching moves that fast. Coverage gaps are a scheduling decision, not a technology limit — know which one you're accepting.

card.headline: Sharper is not the same as sooner
card.sub: A high-resolution image from four days ago cannot show what changed yesterday. Revisit cadence sets what a system can actually see.
